sections.title: Four variables that determine your AI consulting price
sections.description: Understanding these drivers helps you evaluate quotes and scope the right engagement for your needs.

items.title: 1. Consultant Seniority & Track Record
items.description: Rates vary enormously between junior analysts applying templated frameworks and senior practitioners who have actually shipped production AI systems. ClickMasters' rates reflect engineering-backed consulting—the same people who build production systems, not a separate consulting-only staff.
items.label: Experience

items.title: 2. Engagement Scope & Stakeholder Complexity
items.description: A focused assessment for a single department costs less than an organization-wide AI strategy engagement requiring alignment across multiple business units, IT, legal, and executive leadership. Each additional stakeholder group adds meaningful coordination time.
items.label: Scope

items.title: 3. Deliverable Format & Depth
items.description: A lightweight assessment producing a summary memo costs less than a comprehensive strategy document with a detailed implementation roadmap, vendor comparison matrices, and budget modeling. Deliverable depth is scoped explicitly upfront.
items.label: Deliverables

items.title: 4. Industry-Specific Compliance Requirements
items.description: AI governance for regulated industries (healthcare, financial services) typically costs 20–40% more, reflecting the additional regulatory framework knowledge (HIPAA, GDPR, EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, SR 26-2) required to give genuinely useful guidance.
items.label: Compliance

sections.title: What's actually included in an AI consulting engagement
sections.description: Deliverables vary by engagement type, but here's what you can expect for the most common engagements.

blocks.heading: AI opportunity / readiness assessment ($5K–$15K)
paragraphs: Stakeholder interviews to identify candidate use cases; feasibility and ROI assessment for each candidate; data readiness evaluation; and a prioritized recommendation on which use case(s) to pursue first and why.

blocks.heading: Vendor selection & RFP support ($8K–$25K)
paragraphs: Requirements gathering; RFP development or refinement; vendor evaluation criteria; technical evaluation of vendor proposals (including the kind of technical depth a non-technical procurement team often can't assess independently); and a final recommendation with rationale.

blocks.heading: AI strategy & roadmap ($15K–$50K)
paragraphs: Current-state assessment of existing AI/data capabilities; a multi-use-case prioritized roadmap with sequencing rationale; budget and resourcing recommendations; and a presentation to executive stakeholders.

blocks.heading: Fractional AI CTO ($8K–$25K/month)
paragraphs: Ongoing strategic guidance at a defined cadence (weekly or biweekly); vendor and team oversight; technical decision support for in-flight AI initiatives; and availability for ad hoc strategic questions between scheduled sessions—giving organizations without an in-house AI executive access to senior strategic guidance without a full-time hire.

sections.title: When you need consulting—and when you need development

blocks.heading: AI Consulting (Strategy First)
paragraphs: Consulting answers 'what should we build, and is it worth it?'—strategy, feasibility, vendor evaluation, governance. Most organizations benefit from a focused consulting engagement before committing development budget, particularly when the use case or ROI isn't yet well-validated.

blocks.heading: AI Development (Build the Thing)
paragraphs: Development answers 'build the thing'—actual engineering work producing a deployed AI system. A $5,000–$15,000 assessment that concludes a candidate use case isn't worth pursuing is dramatically cheaper than discovering the same conclusion after a $50,000+ development engagement.

sections.title: The questions serious buyers ask before committing to AI consulting
sections.description: No vague promises and no hidden discovery call required to understand the fundamentals.

items.objection: How much will this cost for our specific situation?
items.answer: $5,000–$15,000 for a focused opportunity assessment, $15,000–$50,000 for a full strategy and roadmap engagement, $200–$400/hr for ad hoc advisory. You'll get a fixed quote after an initial scoping conversation that's free and doesn't commit you to anything.
2–4 weeks for assessments, 4–10 weeks for strategy and roadmap development, ongoing for fractional AI CTO retainers. Timeline is defined upfront once scope is clear.

items.objection: Why should I trust your consulting over a cheaper generic consulting firm?
items.answer: Generic management consulting firms applying AI frameworks without engineers who've actually shipped production systems frequently produce strategy documents that look comprehensive but contain technically unrealistic recommendations. ClickMasters' consultants are the same engineers who build production AI systems—strategy reflects what's actually achievable, not theoretical best practice.

items.objection: What happens if your recommendation is that we shouldn't pursue AI for this use case?
items.answer: We'll tell you that directly, and it happens more often than you might expect. An honest assessment from a $5,000–$15,000 consulting engagement saves you from a much larger wasted development investment—and it's why clients return once they see we're not just selling development work regardless of fit.

items.objection: Can you handle our specific industry's regulatory requirements?
items.answer: Yes. ClickMasters' AI consulting practice covers HIPAA, GDPR, the EU AI Act, NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and SR 26-2-aligned governance guidance for financial services—applied based on your specific regulatory exposure during initial scoping.

sections.title: Comparing AI consulting quotes: what to ask

blocks.heading: Headline rates alone don't tell you what you're actually paying for
paragraphs: Ask: who specifically will be doing the work—a senior practitioner with implementation experience, or a junior analyst supervised by someone more senior who won't actually touch your engagement? What does the final deliverable actually look like—a generic templated framework adapted with your company's name, or analysis genuinely specific to your data, systems, and constraints? Does the consultant have direct experience implementing the kind of AI systems being recommended?

blocks.heading: Why a significantly cheaper quote is often cheaper for a reason
paragraphs: A meaningfully cheaper quote is often cheaper because it's staffed by junior analysts applying a generic framework rather than senior practitioners doing genuine situational analysis—which shows up in recommendations that sound reasonable in a slide deck but don't survive contact with your organization's actual technical and operational reality.

sections.title: Questions about AI consulting cost and scope
sections.description: Clear commercial and technical answers before you start.

items.question: Is the initial scoping call itself a paid consulting engagement, or free?
items.answer: Free. ClickMasters' initial consultation is a no-obligation conversation to understand your situation and determine if and what kind of consulting engagement makes sense—you only pay once you decide to move forward with a scoped engagement.

items.question: Do you offer a smaller, lower-cost option for a startup or smaller business?
items.answer: Yes. ClickMasters scopes consulting engagements proportional to organizational size and complexity—a smaller startup's opportunity assessment or strategy engagement costs meaningfully less than an enterprise engagement involving multiple business units and stakeholder groups.

items.question: What's the difference between hourly advisory and a fixed-fee project engagement?
items.answer: Hourly advisory ($200–$400/hr) suits ad hoc questions and ongoing light-touch guidance without a defined deliverable. Fixed-fee engagements suit a defined scope with a specific deliverable (an assessment report, a strategy document) and give you cost certainty upfront rather than open-ended hourly billing.

items.question: Can AI consulting help us evaluate competing vendor proposals we've already received?
items.answer: Yes. Vendor selection support specifically includes technical evaluation of vendor proposals—assessing whether a vendor's proposed approach, timeline, and pricing are technically realistic—even if you've already collected proposals independently and need an informed technical second opinion before committing.

items.question: How is a Fractional AI CTO engagement priced compared to hiring a full-time AI executive?
items.answer: Fractional AI CTO retainers ($8,000–$25,000/month) typically cost a fraction of a full-time AI executive's total compensation ($250,000–$400,000+ annually), making fractional engagement the more accessible option for organizations not yet ready for a full-time senior AI hire.

items.question: Will the consulting engagement try to upsell us into a larger development contract regardless of fit?
items.answer: No—and this is core to ClickMasters' positioning. Our consulting recommendations are based on what genuinely serves your situation, including recommending against AI development when that's the honest assessment, or recommending a smaller-scoped pilot over a large enterprise platform commitment.

items.question: Do you provide ongoing support after the consulting engagement concludes?
items.answer: Most engagements conclude with a defined deliverable. Ongoing support is available through a Fractional AI CTO retainer or ad hoc hourly advisory for organizations wanting continued access to strategic guidance as their AI initiatives progress.

items.question: Can AI consulting help us understand if we're ready for AI, even without existing infrastructure?
items.answer: AI readiness assessment is specifically designed for organizations uncertain whether they have the data, technical infrastructure, and organizational alignment needed to pursue AI successfully—you don't need existing AI infrastructure to benefit.

items.question: Is there a minimum engagement size, or can we book a single hour of advisory time?
items.answer: ClickMasters offers single-hour or short ad hoc advisory sessions at the standard $200–$400/hr rate for organizations with a narrow, specific question that doesn't warrant a full assessment engagement.

sections.title: Case pattern: AI opportunity assessment for a mid-market manufacturer

blocks.heading: From uncertainty to a prioritized $65K development engagement
paragraphs: A mid-market manufacturer's leadership team had heard extensively about AI's potential but had no clear sense of which candidate use case—predictive maintenance, quality inspection computer vision, demand forecasting—would deliver the strongest ROI given their specific operations, data maturity, and budget.

ClickMasters ran a 3-week opportunity assessment ($9,500) involving stakeholder interviews across operations, IT, and finance; a data readiness audit revealing that maintenance logs were sufficiently structured to support a predictive maintenance pilot but quality inspection data wasn't yet usable for computer vision without a multi-month data collection effort; and a final recommendation prioritizing predictive maintenance as the first initiative.
bullets: Revealed clear ROI ranking across use cases
Directly shaped a subsequent $65,000 development project
Gave leadership confidence before committing larger budget

sections.title: Independent vs. vendor-affiliated AI consulting: a real distinction

blocks.heading: The conflict of interest in many AI consulting engagements
paragraphs: Many AI consulting engagements come from vendors who also sell AI development services—a structural conflict of interest, since a consultant whose revenue depends on recommending development work has a built-in incentive to find a reason you need it, regardless of whether it's genuinely the right call.

blocks.heading: How ClickMasters manages this honestly
paragraphs: Our consulting engagements are scoped and priced as standalone deliverables regardless of whether they lead to a subsequent development engagement. We've delivered assessments concluding a client shouldn't pursue AI for their proposed use case—outcomes that cost us a larger potential contract but build the kind of trust that generates repeat engagements and referrals over a longer relationship.

sections.title: Common mistakes organizations make when budgeting for AI consulting

blocks.heading: Skipping consulting and going straight to development
paragraphs: This is the most expensive mistake in AI investment—committing $50,000+ to development before a $5,000–$15,000 assessment would have revealed feasibility or ROI concerns. The asymmetry between assessment cost and development cost makes skipping the assessment a poor bet.

blocks.heading: Hiring a generalist management consulting firm without AI implementation experience
paragraphs: Generic strategy consulting firms can produce comprehensive-looking AI strategy documents without engineers who've actually built production AI systems involved—resulting in recommendations that look thorough on paper but contain technically unrealistic timelines or architectural assumptions.

blocks.heading: Treating a one-time strategy engagement as sufficient for a multi-year journey
paragraphs: A single strategy document produced at one point in time becomes stale as your data maturity, available technology, and competitive landscape evolve. Organizations planning sustained AI investment over multiple years often benefit more from an ongoing Fractional AI CTO retainer.

sections.title: What a strategy & roadmap deliverable actually looks like

blocks.heading: Beyond a generic slide deck
paragraphs: ClickMasters' strategy and roadmap deliverables typically include: a documented current-state assessment of your existing data infrastructure and AI/ML capability maturity; a prioritized list of candidate AI use cases ranked by expected ROI and implementation feasibility; a phased implementation roadmap with realistic timelines; budget and resourcing recommendations including build-vs-buy guidance; and a presentation deck for executive stakeholder alignment.
bullets: Full supporting documentation, not just summary slides

sections.title: How to think about the ROI of AI consulting

blocks.heading: ROI often shows up as cost avoidance
paragraphs: The ROI of a consulting engagement is harder to quantify directly than the ROI of a deployed AI system, since consulting's value often shows up as cost avoidance—not building something that wouldn't have worked—rather than direct revenue or efficiency gain.

An opportunity assessment that prevents even one poorly-fit development engagement pays for itself many times over, given that abandoned or failed AI development projects frequently run $30,000–$150,000+ in sunk cost. Organizations that validate AI use cases through a focused assessment before committing development budget measurably reduce their AI investment failure rate.

sections.title: ClickMasters publishes consulting rates when most firms don't

blocks.heading: Zero of the major consultancies publish AI consulting pricing online
paragraphs: Most AI consulting firms—and especially the major management consultancies offering AI strategy services—require a sales conversation before disclosing even a rough rate, let alone a specific fixed-fee range by engagement type. This opacity makes it difficult for buyers to budget realistically or compare options.

ClickMasters publishes specific rates and engagement-type pricing because consulting scope, like development scope, is genuinely estimable for a practitioner with enough relevant experience—and because pricing transparency is the same competitive differentiator across every page on this site.
